races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF Nursery Handicap (Birdcatcher Series)

runners_data.name: Supreme Lord
runners_data.note: Highest-rated prominent runner (OR 91) with a strong sim-going record of 4/4 on good turf and a recent win at 6f — Donagh O'Connor takes the ride for an in-form trainer at T14 2/13, and the combination of class edge and a natural prominent style makes him the pick of the prominent brigade if he secures clean air early.
runners_data.comment: Supreme Lord won last time out and, returning fit on just nine days' rest, has experience of today's trip and conditions; the 139 lb burden is the one query, but his recent winning form makes him the pick of the field.

runners_data.name: La Tache
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over for G M Lyons after 43 days off, which is the key query, but the sim-going record of 4/4 is compelling and a win at 5f suggests the step back to 6f should suit a horse that was slowly away over this trip last time — the tongue-tie and Keane's positional intelligence could see her slot in nicely at OR 90.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, La Tache arrives at draw eight carrying 138 lb on a compact 43-day break; the main risk is that he was beaten into fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Tradewinds
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for Donnacha O'Brien, fitted with tongue-tie and blindfold, who arrives just 7 days after her last run on the back of a fair run at 6f on good ground — her form figures of 2-3-3 in her better efforts suit a scenario where pace burns off, but she'll need a clean passage from the rear.

runners_data.name: I Ready
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent-style two-year-old with a recent win at 6f on good and a record of 5/6 on sim-going, backed by a claim for apprentice Reese Holohan — the 20-day break is fine, and if she gets a clean berth just off the lead she is capable of running into the placings at OR 84 under a light weight.
runners_data.comment: Ran second last time out and was a winner three starts back, so I Ready arrives in fair nick after a 20-day break, with both distance and going experience in his locker; the 132 lb burden and a mid-table rating of 84 are the checks on his chance.

runners_data.name: Lars Soldier
runners_data.note: Has run consistently in the frame (2nd, 3rd, 4th, 5th) and clearly handles good ground (6/8 on sim-going), but the step back from 8f to 6f is relevant and he arrives just 5 days after his last run — Wesley Joyce (3) rides for a modest yard, and his best chance depends on finding a clear prominent position in a congested race for that spot.
runners_data.comment: Lars Soldier shaped with promise when second three starts back and third five starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, giving him a solid grounding; the concern is he has been winless in recent starts and at 131 lb faces a stiff task on just five days' rest.

runners_data.name: Lady Patrona
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Mrs John Harrington, with Shane Foley engaged and a recent 6f win on good ground to her name — she has the run of the race to herself on the front end and is 5lb clear of her OR-low, making her a genuine factor rather than just a rabbit if the pace is controlled.
runners_data.comment: Lady Patrona arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, while her rating of 93 puts her clear at the head of this field — the chief worry is whether 129 lb from stall one blunts her finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Shesthedevil
runners_data.note: A hold-up type with a genuine win at 6f on good ground in her recent form, but the trainer returns T14 0/5 and the form otherwise has been patchy — Chris Hayes is a quality booking, but from the rear she needs a clear run in what looks a congested mid-race shape.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive sixth-place finishes make Shesthedevil hard to fancy on recent form, and our figures rank her towards the foot of this field, though she does hold a win three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Howlin Wolf
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and has been progressive, winning at 6f on good and placing twice more on sim-going (5/5) — Declan McDonogh is an astute booking for Jack Davison's yard, and as a genuine hold-up runner arriving 9 days fresh, he is the most interesting of the backmarkers if pace is genuine.
runners_data.comment: Howlin Wolf showed his best when winning two starts back, though he was only fourth and seventh in earlier starts before bouncing back into second last time out; he has distance and going experience to draw on, but his speed rating of 61 and ranking seventh of ten suggest he faces a stiff ask from stall three carrying 121 lb.

runners_data.name: Celestial Crown
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by profile but has yet to win or place in five career starts on sim-going — mapped to midfield due to redistribution from the rear as the field has more hold-up types than the map can place, but its natural running style is from the back, which tempers its chance in this scenario-dominant prominent shape, and OR 70 is modest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with three finishes of seventh or worse in that sequence, Celestial Crown is hard to fancy from stall seven carrying 119 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and that familiarity offers modest encouragement.

runners_data.name: Captain James Cook
runners_data.note: An Aidan O'Brien-trained juvenile with only three starts, all mid-division finishes on good ground and a career-best of 6th — a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that position here given the prominent congestion, and with T14 5/35 the yard is not firing at its peak, making improvement hard to project.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Captain James Cook faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and 18 days between runs leaves him fresh enough.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Patrona is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Shane Foley in the saddle for Mrs John Harrington, she is likely to bowl along at a sustainable clip unchallenged on the front end, setting an honest but not suicidal gallop over Navan's flat 6f on good ground. Supreme Lord, La Tache, I Ready, and Lars Soldier all want to race prominently, creating a congested berth for positions two through five, with legitimate traffic danger likely materialising between the 2f and 3f poles as those four jostle for footing. The field holds more prominent-types than the race shape can cleanly accommodate — Lady Patrona is the clear leader, and Supreme Lord (highest OR among the prominent brigade, strong sim-going record) and Colin Keane-ridden La Tache are best-placed to actually secure the prime pitch behind her, while Captain James Cook — a natural prominent racer — is unlikely to find his natural position and has been mapped to midfield. A controlled, honest pace with prominent congestion in the early-to-mid stages strongly favours horses that can travel just off Lady Patrona's shoulder in a clear position — prominent runners with clean air and finishing speed, rather than genuine hold-up horses who will need gaps to open in what promises to be a tightly-bunched back section.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Patrona sets a sustainable gallop and the prominent group settle cleanly just behind her, the race is run to suit runners travelling in the first three or four.
scenarios.body: Lady Patrona controls the tempo without being pressured, and the horses that secure a clear prominent pitch — Supreme Lord and La Tache most obviously — have first run at the 2f pole and can sustain their effort to the line on good ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Two Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes rivals to check or switch, Lady Patrona and whichever horse secures second spot jump clear of a fractured field.
scenarios.body: The early scramble for prominent positions leaves the chasing pack momentarily unbalanced, allowing Lady Patrona to steal an advantage while the horse that slots in cleanly second — likely Supreme Lord — follows her through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scrimmaging burns genuine pace and the sectionals quicken sharply early, the hold-up horses get a genuine target to aim at.
scenarios.body: Tradewinds and Howlin Wolf, both genuine hold-up types with proven good-ground form and capable jockeys, could find daylight down the outside in the final furlong if the pace fractures in front of them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent types take each other on aggressively from the outset and the gallop becomes uncharacteristically hot for a nursery, a midfield tracker benefits from the subsequent stopping.
scenarios.body: Captain James Cook, though racing out of his natural role, and Celestial Crown could profit from a field that has overcookd the pace — though both are redistrubuted runners whose natural positions make this the least reliable outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch Supreme Lord and La Tache for early position — if both attempt to slot directly behind Lady Patrona in the opening furlong, interference is highly likely and one or both could be checked at a critical moment.

Lady Patrona's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the race's central hinge — if she is pushed wider at the break by the prominent cluster, the anticipated controlled pace dissolves and the entire race shape changes.

Howlin Wolf wears a hood and has recorded solid sim-going form — if Declan McDonogh finds a clean passage from the rear in the final furlong, he is the most likely of the hold-up horses to pick off tired prominents in a congested finish.

Lars Soldier arrives just 5 days after his last run — monitor him in the paddock for signs of freshness or flatness, as quick turnarounds for less-fancied yards can occasionally produce bounced performers in two-year-old handicaps.

Captain James Cook and Celestial Crown are both racing out of their natural roles due to redistribution — neither is likely to secure their preferred position, and punters should apply the appropriate discount when assessing their market prices against their true pace profiles.

runners_data.name: Agostino
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse off a 281-day absence — the long layoff is a serious concern, and on similar Going he has only placed 0 times from 3 runs; Jimmy Dalton's 7lb claim helps the burden but the lack of recent racecourse fitness is a major negative.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and absent for 281 days, Agostino faces a stiff task here, though a second three starts back offers some encouragement; carrying 142 lb from stall 10 and rated just 59, he has experience over today's trip and going but must prove his layoff hasn't blunted him.

runners_data.name: Irish Rumour
runners_data.note: Has placed five times from 13 runs on Good ground which gives Orla Tynan (7lb) something to work with, but all recent form has come at 6f-7f and dropping to 5f may not suit a hold-up horse that needs time to wind up.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and second five starts back, Irish Rumour arrives here fit on a 14-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going, and our rating of 65 gives her a case despite carrying 142 lb from stall 14 while yet to score in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Rosato
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the mount on a mare who has placed twice at 6f on Good and ran only 7 days ago — fitness is assured; her prominent style is tailor-made for a slowly run 5f where settling close to Ballysax Lil' Mick could prove decisive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Rosato does bring second-place finishes two and four starts back to suggest she can hit the frame, though unplaced efforts either side temper expectations; she has run over today's trip and going before and runs fresh off a seven-day turnaround carrying 142 lb from stall six.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Good ground and has experience over this exact trip, but her hold-up style leaves her reliant on others to set a true pace in a race where the gallop may not suit her best; 20 days off and visor-free suggests connections are happy with her fitness.
runners_data.comment: Surpass And Shine showed he knows how to win when landing a victory five starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 66 marking him out as a genuine threat from stall nine; the concern is four unplaced runs since that success.

runners_data.name: Asdana
runners_data.note: Visor-fitted hold-up filly whose best effort was a second at 5f on Heacock; form on Good turf at this trip is sparser and she arrives 90 days fresh — the step back up in field size complicates her chances of finding a clear passage late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of nineteen on our rating with a speed figure of 79 that sets her apart from most rivals, Asdana has run over today's trip and going and carries a manageable 141 lb from stall seven, though her recent winless run of five starts — including a pair of unplaced efforts — and a 90-day absence are the key concerns.

runners_data.name: Lethimfly
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a major booking for a hold-up horse who has been running consistently in this sort of grade, but six finishes of 10th or worse from recent outings and a 0/12 record without a placed finish on Good ground are damning; needs everything to go right from the back.
runners_data.comment: Lethimfly catches the eye as the top-rated runner in the field, and having run over today's trip and going he arrives with course-relevant experience; yet to score in his last five starts, and that winless run of form is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Simmering Seas
runners_data.note: Ben Coen's mount has placed twice from seven runs on Good ground over 5f-6f, and while naturally a hold-up type, her recent form shows genuine finishing kick; the 3-year-old age allowance means she carries one of the lighter weights in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Simmering Seas nonetheless brings solid placed form — second last time out and a second three starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 140 lb from stall 15 are factors to weigh against her.

runners_data.name: Steel Magnolia
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good ground 13 days ago and clearly in form — her prominent style puts her ideally placed in this race shape, and the McCreery yard is red-hot with six winners from 19 runners in the past 14 days; must be respected.
runners_data.comment: Steel Magnolia won last time out and was second two starts back, giving her a sharp upward curve in form, though a seventh three starts back tempers expectations; experience over today's trip and going helps, but 138 lb from stall 17 is no easy ask.

runners_data.name: One Cool Bear
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness has been striking at a 13% clip over 14 days; however, this horse is a genuine hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot purely by the numbers in this field, meaning it is unlikely to secure its ideal position — discount accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and returning after 85 days off, One Cool Bear faces questions about fitness, yet he has run over today's distance and going before and carries 137 lb from stall three, with our rating of 62 suggesting he holds a little more in reserve than his official mark implies.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 6f on Good ground gives Glen Breeze form credentials, but it is naturally a come-from-behind horse that will struggle to replicate the position it won from in a field this size; Shane Markey's 7lb claim softens the weight but not the positional problem.
runners_data.comment: Glen Breeze won four starts back but has posted a sixth, fifth and ninth in his last three outings, suggesting he may be hard to catch right now; he has run over today's trip and going before, though the quick five-day turnaround is a concern.

runners_data.name: Caffu Zafeen
runners_data.note: Form figures of 14-9-11-15-18 on Good ground tell an unambiguous story — this is a horse that rarely gets involved at the business end, and with its natural hold-up style further compromised by the crowded rear of the field, prospects look slim.
runners_data.comment: Caffu Zafeen has run over today's trip and going, yet he has been winless in his last five starts with a best recent effort of ninth, and 132 lb from stall 19 makes things no easier for a gelding rated 49 on official figures.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra Dream
runners_data.note: 239-day layoff is a red flag, the form line is limited to three runs at longer trips, and the ⚠ fade flag suggests it stops when the race quickens; it is a genuine hold-up type already mapped away from its natural territory, which compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and absent for 239 days, Cleopatra Dream faces a stiff task on these figures as the 15th-ranked of 19 runners, though she has run over today's trip and carries a clear weight.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Has won and placed at 6f on Good but the ⚠ fade warning and a 50-day break make it hard to trust; its hold-up style is its natural weapon yet the redistribution away from the rear means it will need luck in running that cannot be guaranteed in a 19-runner sprint.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Monastere faces a stiff task returning from 50 days off and after finishing ninth last time out, though he has experience of today's trip and conditions and did score three starts back.

runners_data.name: Ballysax Lil' Mick
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front runner in the field — an 8-year-old gelding off 20 days who has led and placed on Good ground previously; the task is to control tempo rather than burn them off, and with no pressure likely early, Wesley Joyce can nurse this horse to the line.
runners_data.comment: Ballysax Lil' Mick has run over today's trip and going before, and 20 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, but he is winless in his last five starts and his official mark of 43 makes the task look stiff from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Step Back In Time
runners_data.note: Two wins from 14 runs on Good ground and a third 13 days ago shows this veteran is in excellent fettle; his prominent style suits this race shape precisely, Gary Carroll is experienced at riding these sprint handicaps, and the low weight of 126lbs is an asset.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 14th of 19 on our figures, Step Back In Time faces a stiff task here; a third two starts back offers the slender consolation, and she has run over today's trip and going before, returning on a quick 13-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Kidd
runners_data.note: Only three career runs and the ⚠ fade flag mark this as the most unexposed runner in the field; a genuine hold-up type that has shown no evidence of the finishing burst needed to win from deep in a 19-runner field, and the redistribution reduces its chances further.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Kidd faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going, and a 49-day break at least means she arrives fresh, but her recent unplaced efforts make her hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: The Love Machine
runners_data.note: Showed a flash of form with a fifth at 5f on Soft 31 days ago, but previous runs on Good ground are uninspiring; naturally a hold-up horse that needs the pace to be strong enough to reel in the prominently placed horses — which in this race looks unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, The Love Machine does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and his 31-day break gives connections time to have him spot-on; 124 lb from stall 18 make it hard to fancy him strongly, however.

runners_data.name: Jackandthefox
runners_data.note: Jennifer Anne Lynch's second runner here; a consistent prominent type who has placed five times in his last six races at 5f-6f on Good ground, carrying 123lbs is manageable, and Rory Cleary is a capable handler who can place him close enough to matter.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 16 of 19 on our figures, Jackandthefox is hard to fancy despite the fitness edge of a 33-day break; he has run over today's trip and going before, but consistent near-miss finishes without threatening suggest improvement is needed.

runners_data.name: Lismacbryan
runners_data.note: ⚠ fade flag and form figures of 19-7-17-14-8 paint a bleak picture; this mare is a hold-up horse already shuffled away from the back of the field by the numbers, and her visor has not unlocked anything convincing at this trip on Good ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 18 of 19 on our figures, Lismacbryan is hard to fancy on recent form, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a handy 13-day turnaround from draw 1.

races.paceDynamic: Ballysax Lil' Mick is the lone confirmed front runner in a 19-runner field and, with no genuine challenger likely to press hard from the outset on Good ground over 5f at Navan, should be able to control tempo at a sustainable rather than breakneck gallop. Step Back In Time and Rosato are the natural prominent types best placed to track the leader through the early exchanges, with Steel Magnolia and Jackandthefox also capable of sitting just off the pace if they get a clear run from their draws. This field carries a heavy concentration of hold-up horses — One Cool Bear, Glen Breeze, Caffu Zafeen, Cleopatra Dream, Monastere, Kidd, The Love Machine, and Lismacbryan are all genuine come-from-behind types who are redistributed to midfield on the map simply because there are far more hold-up horses than the race can accommodate at the rear; in practice, the riders on these horses will be jostling for similar ground and several will inevitably end up wider and further back than ideal. A controlled, single-pace gallop set by Ballysax Lil' Mick strongly favours horses who can sit close to the action early — prominent and stalking types who do not need a strong pace to fire — rather than the overcrowded hold-up brigade who will need a stronger gallop to generate the closing kick their style demands.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Ballysax Lil' Mick finds a comfortable lead unchallenged and the large field creates enough interference to bottle up the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Ballysax Lil' Mick dictates at a sustainable clip through the 5f on Good ground, and with 19 runners creating traffic for closers, the prominent horses sitting just behind can pounce without burning much energy; this shape massively advantages horses who get an unobstructed rail position near the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Step Back In Time or Rosato press close enough to the pace to strike decisively inside the final furlong while the lone front runner fades.
scenarios.body: With a solo leader dictating a measured pace, the horses positioned just off the shoulder get the perfect draught and can accelerate past in the closing stages on this flat 5f track; this scenario rewards prominent types with proven Good-ground form at the trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the middle stages to string the field out and create a clear lane for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A horse like Simmering Seas or Asdana, who have placed on Good ground at this trip, finds a gap as the field spreads, but this outcome is hampered by the sheer number of redistributed hold-up types competing for the same late run; execution risk is high with 19 runners and a restrained gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Elevates Rank Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant trouble in running, bunching the mid-division and allowing a lightly-weighted, fresh horse to exploit the carnage from an uncontested position.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up horses reshuffled out of their natural roles and jostling for space, interference in the closing stages could open a gap for a horse like Monastere or Glen Breeze that finds daylight by luck rather than design; this is the most speculative shape and depends entirely on positional misfortune elsewhere.

watchPoints.text: Steel Magnolia and Step Back In Time are both on form and prominent-style — watch whether either gets the rail position behind Ballysax Lil' Mick, as the horse that does is perfectly placed to pounce.

With at least eight genuine hold-up horses redistributed into mid-division, watch for a bunched, traffic-heavy closing furlong where several of these runners — especially One Cool Bear and Glen Breeze — will be looking for gaps that may not materialise.

Ballysax Lil' Mick's ability to maintain its lead depends entirely on not being pressured early — watch the first furlong to see if Step Back In Time or any other prominent type moves up to challenge; if they do, the pace dynamic changes sharply.
Rosato ran just seven days ago and is tackling 5f instead of her usual 6f — watch her early to see if Shane Foley sends her forward aggressively to use that recent fitness edge or sits and waits.

McCreery has Steel Magnolia and Asdana in the same race — watch for any signs of stable jockey preference, as W J Lee rides Steel Magnolia (the more fancied of the two given recent form), suggesting that is the yard's primary hope.

races.name: Christmas Parties At Navan Racecourse On 6th & 13th December Handicap

runners_data.name: Erosandpsyche
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with six placed efforts from 14 runs on similar going, handled by a 7lb claimer; the 6-day turnaround and tongue-tie/hood combination is consistent with a yard managing a horse in form, but needs genuine pace to close into.|
runners_data.comment: Erosandpsyche ran second last time out and is back quickly on six days' rest, which speaks to his wellbeing, and he has run over today's trip and going before; yet to win in recent starts, but drawn four carrying 140 lb, his overall profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Thunderbear
runners_data.note: 77 days off the track is the primary concern here — Stephen Thorne has only 1 winner from 3 runners in the last 14 days, and this hold-up type needs a strongly run race to produce his best; his sole Good-going win came over 6f, making the 5f trip a minor additional query.|
runners_data.comment: Thunderbear warrants plenty of respect — rated 103 and ranked top of the field here, he has a win in his last five starts and brings both distance and going experience to the table, though his two most recent unplaced efforts and a 77-day absence are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Amiata
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes a notable booking and this three-year-old has won four of her last six, including on Good and over 5f, giving her strong profile credentials — however, her natural trailing style means she is being asked to race closer to the pace than ideal, which tempers the case for her in a scenario defined by a controlled gallop.|
runners_data.comment: Amiata arrives on the back of a win nine days ago and has won three times in his last six starts, showing a reliable winning thread; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 130 lb is the one factor that could blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Namiid
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rode this horse to its last win and retains the partnership; the consistent prominent racing style (headgear: p) and five runs at this exact trip on Good ground (11/13 sim-going) make Namiid one of the best-placed horses to exploit the clean pace set by Allsortz, with no tactical question marks.|
runners_data.comment: Placed on each of his last two starts, with a win four starts back giving his recent form a solid foundation, Namiid has experience of today's trip and conditions and his 86 rating suggests he holds clear claims; the 49-day absence is the one thing to take on trust.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: The only horse mapped to lead and carries the race shape on its shoulders; has won over 5f on Soft, form over Good is modest (0W2P), and Luke McAteer is a journeyman booking rather than a confidence signal from the Marnane yard — the tactical advantage is real but the raw form is limited.|

runners_data.name: Moltophino
runners_data.note: Prominent type with tongue-tie/breast-girth, running off a low base of 76 OR but four of last five runs on Good going returned finishes of 9th or worse — Chris Hayes in the saddle is an upgrade in class but the form line does not inspire confidence even in a shape that theoretically suits.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Moltophino at least showed encouragement with a runner-up finish last time out, 14 days ago, and he has run over today's distance and going before; carrying 119 lb from stall eight, a rating of 83 suggests he retains ability, though consistency remains the question.

runners_data.name: Gotta Catch'em All
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose last two wins came from the rear but who cannot get that position in this race; the 3-day turnaround and blinkered headgear suggest connections are trying to find an edge, but being unable to drop out and finish late as intended materially weakens the case here.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and returning just three days after his last outing, Gotta Catch'em All faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and showed a third two starts back among recent form that also includes a couple of wins.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a form string of five consecutive 0s and positional finishes of 12th to 18th across recent runs — even in an ideal scenario where closers flourish, this horse's raw ability appears stretched at OR 72; the redistribution away from its natural rear position adds another layer of difficulty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Dandyville is hard to fancy despite returning quickly just three days ago; he has run over today's distance and going before, and stall three is his draw.

races.paceDynamic: Allsortz is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to stride out and control pace from the front without being pressed — a sustainable, even gallop over 5f on Good ground at Navan suits a horse who can bowl along and idle. Namiid and Moltophino will push forward to take up prominent positions just behind the leader, creating a small, organised group that sets a clean but not brutal tempo. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Amiata, Gotta Catch'em All, and Dandyville are all genuine closers but at least one or two will be unable to drop out as far as they prefer, meaning the rear of the field may not form the deep pocket of late pace that true hold-up scenarios require. A controlled, uncontested lead with modest early fractions on Good turf over this sprint trip strongly favours prominent racers who can travel close to the gallop and pick off the leader inside the final furlong, rather than horses needing a strong pace to reel in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Allsortz Controls, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz dictates a fair but uncontested pace and the prominent horses track him without incident.
scenarios.body: Allsortz rolls along at the front and the race develops steadily, giving Namiid and Moltophino every chance to advance on even terms around the 2f pole before the sprint unfolds; in a race without a searching gallop, horses racing just off the pace hold a decisive positional edge into the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz establishes a comfortable lead and uses Good ground to maintain his gallop all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: With no horse able to apply pressure, Allsortz can dictate his own rhythm and avoid the energy-sapping battles that often kill off front-runners in sprint handicaps; a strong finish from a horse who has won from the front and who has a clear run in trip and going conditions becomes plausible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than expected and the front runners come back to the genuine hold-up horses in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Amiata is a high-class finisher whose four wins and strong form suggest she can produce a late burst if conditions allow, but her redistribution to midfield means she is unlikely to get the true rear position and late swoop that makes this scenario work; Erosandpsyche has prominent placed form at this trip on Good but similarly needs more of a test of pace than one front-runner typically provides.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Collapses Into Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent racer breaks sharply and challenges Allsortz for the lead, igniting an unplanned duel and turning the race into a test of stamina.
scenarios.body: An unexpected pace battle would scramble the tactical order and could see the better-bred hold-up types benefit from a fast-run 5f on Good ground, but none of the field's redistrubuted closers are well-placed to capitalise on this given their likely midfield berths rather than a genuine hold-up position.

watchPoints.text: Watch Namiid's early position — if Ben Coen travels prominently and smoothly in second or third behind Allsortz, this horse is ideally placed for the race shape that is most likely to develop.

Monitor Amiata at the start — if Colin Keane instinctively drops her out to her natural hold-up position rather than committing forward, she will be racing in her comfort zone but will need the pace to lift sharply in the final furlong to get home.

Allsortz's recent Good-going form (0 wins, 2 places) is weaker than the leading role demands — if she shows any signs of stopping inside the final furlong, every prominent horse immediately behind becomes a beneficiary.

Thunderbear's 77-day absence is worth monitoring in the first furlong — a hold-up type who is ring-rusty may drift further back than intended and find himself completely out of contention in a race run at a sound but not fast pace.

Dandyville has finished last or near-last in all five recent starts and is a legitimate non-runner risk in terms of competitive danger — watch whether Rory Cleary attempts to find a prominent pitch to compensate for the crowded hold-up sector.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Return Of The Jumps At Navan Racecourse September 19th Handicap (Div I)

runners_data.name: Albatala
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Soft and placed on Good, now steps back up to 1m2f where his best form sits; Sam Coen's 5lb claim is useful in a competitive handicap and the prominent style suits this controlled-pace shape perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Albatala won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a balanced profile, though 55 days off the track introduces a fitness query and she faces 23 rivals carrying 142 lb from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up mare with 0 wins and just one place from 12 recent runs on Good — deep form figures do not inspire and the trip is on the sharp side of her stamina range.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Katherine arrives here on a quick ten-day turnaround carrying 142 lb from stall one, and while she has run over today's trip before, her recent string of unplaced efforts makes improvement essential.

runners_data.name: Pallatine Hills
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been racing almost exclusively at sprint distances of 8-9f; stepping up to 10f for the first time on Good ground represents an untested stamina question with no evidence she gets the trip.
runners_data.comment: Pallatine Hills brings strong claims here, ranked second of 24 on our rating with a speed figure of 76 to his name, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that he is winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: God Knows
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose best figures have come over 7-8f; career win came on Good but has gone 0W from 10 recent runs at similar trips, and the step to 1m2f looks a stretch based on his form profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, God Knows nonetheless carries a rating of 77 — top of 24 runners — and returns on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's distance and going to call on; she maps as the one to beat despite her recent struggles.

runners_data.name: Make The Tide
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Good recently but is a genuine hold-up horse racing only 3 days after his last run; the redistribution into midfield means he will not get his natural rear-positioned role, and at 1m2f he is untested over this longer trip.
runners_data.comment: Make The Tide rates 62 on our figures, fourth-best of these, and bounced back to score last time out, giving her strong claims fresh from just three days ago; the main concern is whether that quick turnaround blunts her finishing effort here.

runners_data.name: Neon Eyes
runners_data.note: Showed a clear ability to finish close at 10f on Good when second last time, and Gavin Cromwell has him fresh off 73 days; the hold-up style is genuine but a clear run in this traffic-heavy field will be the deciding factor.
runners_data.comment: Neon Eyes shaped with promise when a close second two starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going in her favour, but a 73-day absence combined with a trainer hitting only 5% in the last 14 days makes confidence harder to hold.

runners_data.name: African Affair
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and only three career starts, all showing nothing above eighth; 110 days off and no evidence she handles 10f make this a speculative entry.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and absent for 110 days, African Affair arrives short of recent encouragement, though he has run over today's distance and going before and carries a manageable 133 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Alto Sax
runners_data.note: Has won at 8f on Good and placed twice, including at 12f, so the trip suits; a true hold-up runner forced into midfield by redistribution, and though the style fit is slightly compromised the 9-day turnaround is fine for Peter Fahey.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner six starts back, Alto Sax brings distance and going experience to the table and his our rating edges above his official mark, but that ninth two starts back is a concern and 133 lb is no featherweight ask.

runners_data.name: Jazz Forever
runners_data.note: Prominent style with a fades-in-finish flag and recent form figures of 0-0-0 at distances beyond 12f; the Good ground is fine but the recent record suggests this is a difficult assignment.
runners_data.comment: Jazz Forever has run over today's trip and going before, but winless in his last six starts with three consecutive unplaced efforts weighing against him; third four starts back offers some encouragement, and at 133 lb from stall three he has conditions to work with.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and therefore the architect of the entire race shape; Shane Foley can dictate fully unchallenged, and while she has yet to win she has shown consistent staying form at 10-14f on Good going for K J Condon.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Mare Crisium has nonetheless shown consistency with a pair of fourths in recent outings and has experience of today's trip and conditions; 133 lb from stall 14 is the challenge as she tries to edge forward from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Nephin Mountain
runners_data.note: Won at 8f and 10f on Good for Michael Mulvany, and the hold-up style belies a strong record of placing; Wesley Joyce's stablemate Cause I Like You means pace orders could interfere, but his 10f winning form on Good is directly relevant here.
runners_data.comment: Nephin Mountain won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going in his favour, but carrying 133 lb from stall 19 and an official rating of 57 with patchy recent form — two wins and three disappointing efforts in his last six starts — suggests he is not without risks.

runners_data.name: Wipeawayyourtears
runners_data.note: Won at 12f on Good and placed twice over 10f on Good and Soft — the trip and going are squarely in his wheelhouse; the hold-up style is genuine and the 5-day turnaround is short but connections clearly have him ready.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and filled the frame twice in recent starts, but she comes into this unplaced last time out, just five days on, and a high weight of 133 lb from stall 23 tests her stamina in a competitive 24-runner field.

runners_data.name: Calamint
runners_data.note: Showed a place at 10f on Good and third at 10f on Soft; a true hold-up runner redistributed into midfield by the field size, and while the style fit is marginally compromised the course-and-distance profile is solid for Adrian Murray.

runners_data.name: Oh I Do Declare
runners_data.note: Only three career runs, all showing figures of 9th or worse, with fades-in-finish pattern evident; laid off 143 days and is a natural hold-up type who will not get near his preferred position in a 24-runner field — very hard to enthuse about.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, the most recent of which came 143 days ago, Oh I Do Declare heads into this off the back of a ninth and two unplaced efforts, and our rating of 48 ranks him 19th of 24 — though he has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the low-teens in handicap company, with a fade-in-finish flag and zero wins or places from five career runs; the true hold-up style cannot be accommodated in this congested field and the form gives no reason to believe in improvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 20th of 24 on our figures, Chloe's Boy faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Eight runs and zero wins or places across trips from 7-10f on Good — the fade-in-finish flag is supported by the form, and being pushed out of the rear position in this redistribution makes the task even harder.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Kingcharles has struggled for consistency, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround from stall five carrying 129 lb; our rating of 58 suggests a shade more ability than his official mark of 53 implies.

runners_data.name: Churchill Gale
runners_data.note: Returning from 304 days off for Dermot McLoughlin; showed ability to place at 10-11f on Good but the lengthy absence and redistribution away from the hold-up position he favours make him a significant risk at this stage of training.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for over 300 days, Churchill Gale faces a stiff task from stall 20 carrying 126 lb, and her finishing positions offer little encouragement — though she has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: De Songbird
runners_data.note: Six runs on Good with a best finish of sixth at 10f — the form figures do not suggest this 1m2f trip is within reach, and being displaced from the rear position in a large field compounds the difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, De Songbird has struggled for consistency, though she has run over today's distance and going before and comes here on a sharp 14-day turnaround; carrying 125 lb from stall 11, she remains one to watch rather than follow blindly at this stage.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is an asset and this horse has placed multiple times at 8f on Good, including a win; however the step to 10f is unproven and as a natural hold-up type forced into midfield the style fit is compromised.
runners_data.comment: Ranked 18th of 24 on our figures, Cause I Like You faces a stiff task on these ratings, though she was a winner three starts back and filled the runner-up spot last time out, suggesting some residual form to cling to; the return after just six days is the main query.

runners_data.name: Miss Ivor
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in the 9th-12th range at trips of 7-12f on Good with a fade-in-finish flag and zero success; the redistribution away from her preferred hold-up role in a 24-runner field compounds an already uninspiring profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Miss Ivor faces a stiff task here; she does return on a short turnaround with going experience in her favour, but her recent string of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy her chances.

runners_data.name: Capall Cuain
runners_data.note: Three runs, three finishes of 13th, 15th and 14th — the form is uniformly poor and the fade-in-finish flag is consistent with those figures; a natural hold-up type who will trail the field in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Capall Cuain faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's going before and 18 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a fade-in-finish flag and best recent finish of sixth at 13f on Good; an amateur jockey reservation and redistribution from rear to midfield make it very hard to see a pathway into contention.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 23 of 24 on our figures, Bang Po faces a stiff task here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a relatively quick turnaround of 11 days, but little else in his recent profile invites confidence.

runners_data.name: Haeret In Pectore
runners_data.note: Returning from 125 days off for A J Martin; has placed at 10f on Soft but is operating from a reserve jockey slot and the redistribution out of a true hold-up position weakens any case for involvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 22 of 24 on our figures, Haeret In Pectore arrives 125 days between runs and faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before and retains a featherweight 122 lb.

runners_data.name: Giselles Defence
runners_data.note: Has a win at 8f on Good and placed at 13f, suggesting some stamina range; operating on a reserve jockey and having raced only 3 days ago, the natural hold-up style placed into midfield leaves this horse needing a lot to go right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and back just three days after his most recent unplaced effort, Giselles Defence faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 61 offers a sliver of encouragement from stall 15 carrying 134 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Mare Crisium is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 24-runner field and, with no other genuine leader to press her, Shane Foley can dictate a controlled, honest gallop from the front — sustainable enough that she will not be setting herself alight, but real enough to avoid a false-pace scramble. The congestion behind her is significant: Oh I Do Declare, Make The Tide, Kingcharles, Churchill Gale and several others are natural prominent or hold-up types who will find their preferred positions compressed by the sheer size of the field, forcing many to race in unfamiliar midfield slots. That redistribution means the race is likely to be run as a single-file, evenly-strung contest with a genuine pace from the front and a wall of horses hunting Mare Crisium from two furlongs out. This race shape — honest gallop, no injection of false pace, no late dawdle — strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the leader and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, particularly those with proven form at this trip and in Good conditions; hold-up horses squeezed back beyond their natural position face a compounded task.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mare Crisium Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and the large field fails to close the gap until too late.
scenarios.body: Mare Crisium settles into her natural front-running rhythm under Shane Foley, and with no genuine challenger for the lead she sets a metronomic pace that suits her stamina profile at 1m2f on Good ground; the congested midfield takes time to organise itself leaving her with a decisive advantage entering the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If horses racing just behind Mare Crisium track her seamlessly and produce a stronger finishing effort through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Albatala and Nephin Mountain, both racing prominently in a field where the pace is genuine, get the ideal tow into contention without burning unnecessary energy; with the field strung out behind them they face clear daylight from two furlongs out and can sustain their runs without traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find a Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race and the front group ties itself up, leaving a fractional gap for midfield runners to burst through.
scenarios.body: Wipeawayyourtears and Neon Eyes, who have genuine staying form at this distance and good Going form, are best equipped among the hold-up contingent to exploit a collapse in the leaders; however most true hold-up runners have been redistributed into midfield and will not be in a clean position to launch a sustained run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field clusters together due to a slow early tempo and the race degenerates into a sprint finish from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish in a 24-runner field on a tight final straight creates random traffic scenarios and benefits any horse with a sharp turn of foot over a short distance; this is the least likely shape given Mare Crisium's confirmed front-running role and the genuine pace she is expected to set.

watchPoints.text: Mare Crisium (Shane Foley) is completely uncontested for the lead — if she gets a soft lead at a comfortable tempo she becomes very hard to peg back in a 24-runner field where the chasers must organise themselves through heavy traffic.

Nephin Mountain and Cause I Like You share the same trainer (Michael Mulvany) and jockey pairing could influence running tactics — watch for any team orders that affect which horse is ridden to win and which offers cover.

Wipeawayyourtears ran only 5 days ago; if that quick turnaround has left him below peak freshness his strong 12f form on Good could be deceiving, and he needs a trouble-free passage from a midfield position in a 24-runner field.

With 24 runners on a 1m2f flat course at Navan, early position on the rail will be fiercely contested — horses drawn widest who need prominent positions (Albatala, Jazz Forever) face extra ground at the start before the first bend organises the field.

Neon Eyes is 73 days fresh for Gavin Cromwell who has a live 14-day strike rate of 2/39 — watch for any market support that suggests the stable has him ready despite the absence, as his second at 10f on Good last time is the best recent form in this field.

races.name: Return Of The Jumps At Navan Racecourse September 19th Handicap (Div II)

runners_data.name: Nibras Rainbow
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front runner here, has recent Good-ground form and a blinker edge; holds a STYLE_FIT note suggesting it is racing slightly out of role but as the race's sole pace-setter it is actually best placed to exploit the shape it creates — watch for a bold front-running display.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner four starts back, Nibras Rainbow has shown he can compete at this level, but a ninth two starts back tempers enthusiasm; he has run over today's trip and going, and 142 lb is no small ask from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Miss Crinshawn
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey's hold-up mare was last seen just 9 days ago, carries a hood, and her best form has come over trips around 10-12f on Good ground; Ben Coen rides and she will need a searching gallop and a clean run to deliver her finish in a field this large.
runners_data.comment: Placed third three starts back and second five starts back, Miss Crinshawn arrives here quickly on nine days' rest with experience over today's trip and going, and her rating of 60 ranks her among the chief dangers in a 24-runner field; the risk is that she remains winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Ballaghkeen
runners_data.note: Bolger runner returning from a 323-day absence, which is a major flag; limited Good-ground form at this trip and the lengthy layoff makes assessment of current fitness near-impossible — treat with caution despite the yard's occasional ability to produce fit first-timers back.
runners_data.comment: Ballaghkeen is yet to score in her last four starts and returns after a 323-day absence, which is a significant unknown, though she has run over today's going before and carries a manageable 138 lb from stall 17.

runners_data.name: Keilah
runners_data.note: A six-year-old hold-up type wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, with some solid Good-going form over 10f; ran a good race last time and the 24-day break is fine, but needs genuine pace to find her finish in a field where the tempo may not be strong enough.

runners_data.name: Millhone
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's three-year-old has an excellent recent record of placing (four seconds in five runs) over 10-14f on Good ground; Rory Mulligan (5) in the saddle, and the consistent finishing profile suits if she can get daylight late — one of the more reliable form figures in the race.
runners_data.comment: Millhone has been a model of consistency, placing in four of her last six starts with a second last time out and a third two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going holds her in good stead; the main concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Deuteronomy
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns rides this seven-year-old who has a "fades in finish" flag and carries a redistribution note — his true hold-up style cannot be accommodated at the rear in this field, so he'll be forced midfield and his tendency to fade at the end of races makes his task harder from that position.

runners_data.name: Strike De Vega
runners_data.note: Adrian Oliver's three-year-old has a "fades in finish" flag and very modest recent form (0600); Good-ground form has been poor and the step up in this competitive field looks unlikely to reverse the trend.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 18th of 24 on our figures, Strike De Vega faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick nine-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Queen Leila
runners_data.note: Won over 8f at Sligo on Yielding ground but all her form is on artificial or sharp tracks; this flat 1m2f Good ground at Navan over a longer trip represents a very different test and her sim-going figures (2/11) do not inspire confidence.
runners_data.comment: Showed she can win when scoring two starts back, but has since disappointed, finishing unplaced last time out; has run over today's going before and returns after 21 days, though her official mark of 55 suggests she faces a stiff task from the field.

runners_data.name: Tickle The Cat
runners_data.note: Kevin Coleman's three-year-old has the "fades in finish" flag and recent form reads 0807 — nothing to recommend at this level and this trip looks on the edge of their stamina comfort zone based on recent runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked 19th of 24 on our figures, Tickle The Cat faces a stiff task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 21-day break.

runners_data.name: Trishuli River
runners_data.note: Shane Crawley's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up type who has been remapped to midfield due to the volume of closers in this field; wore a tongue-tie, and while he has placed on Good ground over 12-13f before, the style displacement and a 47-day absence temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Trishuli River tops our ratings in a wide-open field and has experience of today's trip and conditions, yet her recent string of unplaced efforts — including eighth last time out, 47 days ago — is the obvious concern for a mare still winless in her last six starts.

runners_data.name: Captain Con
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a major positive, but this Noel Meade three-year-old carries both a "fades in finish" flag and a redistribution note; has been off 63 days and all recent efforts have been poor — Keane's quality alone cannot overcome those structural negatives.
runners_data.comment: Captain Con is winless in his last five starts and returns after 63 days off with a trainer who has yet to land a winner from 24 runners in the past fortnight, making it hard to fancy his claims despite having run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Thegooseiscooked
runners_data.note: Gerard Keane's nine-year-old has won at 10f on Good ground and placed at the same trip; Jack Kearney (3) rides, and while he is a genuine hold-up performer, the redistribution to midfield still leaves him capable of finding a position in a true closing role if there's a gap — perhaps marginally less compromised than some others remapped here.
runners_data.comment: Thegooseiscooked has run over today's trip and going, but she arrives winless in her last five starts, with only a third two runs back to show, and 129 lb from stall 19 adds further burden to a mare who will need to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Morning Approach
runners_data.note: W McCreery's eight-year-old has the "fades in finish" flag and a dispiriting recent form string (506000); the trainer's 14-day strike rate is notably active (6/19) but the horse's own evidence strongly argues against optimism regardless of stable form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Morning Approach has run over today's trip and going before, and 22 days between runs suggests she comes here reasonably fresh; however, a sequence of unplaced efforts makes improvement hard to identify at a rating of 44.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's three-year-old is a genuine prominent racer who should secure a position near the pace; wore a tongue-tie and has Good-ground form over this trip — Terry Casey (7) is the booking, and if the pace is honest this horse could prove durable enough to feature in the finish.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Borora Aura arrives on a quick nine-day turnaround and has run over today's trip and going, though an unplaced effort last time and a run-of-the-mill rating of 49 suggest she faces a stiff task from stall 11 carrying 127 lb.

runners_data.name: He Knows When
runners_data.note: Returning from an extraordinary 784-day absence, which is an enormous unknown; his pre-absence form showed consistent prominent placing at 9-10f on Good ground, and if fitness is there after the long layoff he is naturally placed to exploit this race shape — but the gap in time demands a significant leap of faith.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after a lengthy 784-day absence, He Knows When faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a third two starts back offers a hint of ability.

runners_data.name: Emily's Boy
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's three-year-old has been off 147 days and carries both a "fades in finish" tag and a redistribution note; all previous form has been on softer or artificial surfaces — Good ground at 1m2f looks a difficult assignment on multiple counts.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Emily's Boy has been off the track for 147 days and, ranked last on our figures, makes little appeal on these terms despite carrying 125 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Patrick Magee's three-year-old has a "fades in finish" flag and has been displaced from a true hold-up role to midfield; placed at 13f on Good ground before, and wears a tongue-tie, but the redistribution note and finishing tendency limit appeal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 17th of 24 on our figures, Wingit faces a stiff task here; an unplaced last time does little to inspire confidence, though she has run over today's distance and going before and 21 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Mulvany's other runner, just 6 days since last run; has the "fades in finish" flag and has been pushed out of a true closing role by the field's composition — placed at 10f on Good ground but the very quick turnaround and style displacement combine to create doubt.
runners_data.comment: Arizona Star has been winless in her last five starts and ranks 20th of 24 on our figures, making her very hard to fancy, though she has run over today's distance and going before and an eighth last time out at least shows recent racecourse experience.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Ian Donoghue's three-year-old has never managed better than sixth in six career starts, all on Good ground at shorter trips; wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and the form figures (786987) tell a clear story about the level of performance to date.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and carrying 122 lb from stall 23, Due In June faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's going before and a return just six days ago suggests connections are keen.

runners_data.name: Connova
runners_data.note: Sheila Lavery's three-year-old has a tidy record of placed efforts (four in five at 10f on Good) and a 14-day active trainer; remapped to midfield from a true hold-up role, but the consistency of their form book makes them one of the more credible closers in this field if a gap appears.
runners_data.comment: Connova has shown consistent form of late, placing third two and three starts back, and returns here on a quick turnaround of 24 days with experience of today's trip and conditions working in her favour; winless in her last five starts, she maps well on our figures and runs off an official rating of 43.

runners_data.name: Cadreville
runners_data.note: Jarlath Fahey's three-year-old wears a hood and has been building in distance — best recent effort was 3rd over 10f on Good; Nathan Crosse rides and the redistribution to midfield from a hold-up role is less damaging for a horse already showing some tactical flexibility in their runs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well towards the foot of the field on our figures, Cadreville is a tough one to fancy, though he has run over today's trip and going before and at least returns on a feasible 43-day break.

runners_data.name: Sunny Dude
runners_data.note: D Buckley's six-year-old has been off 61 days and recent form (40076-) is discouraging; the "fades in finish" flag is compounded by being displaced from the hold-up berth they need, and previous form has mainly been over much longer trips than 1m2f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Sunny Dude has been out of form throughout recent starts, and 61 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 124 lb is manageable, but it is hard to make a case from stall 20.

runners_data.name: Carrickfinn
runners_data.note: Shane Gallagher's seven-year-old has been absent 125 days and carries both a "fades in finish" flag and a redistribution note; all recent form has been on Soft or Standard surfaces, and Good ground at Navan over this trip is a very different proposition — the combination of factors makes assessment extremely difficult.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Carrickfinn has been consistently out of the frame and returns after 125 days off, making him very hard to fancy here despite having experience over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Onyeisi
runners_data.note: Karl Thornton's three-year-old ran just 3 days ago, which is an extremely quick turnaround; the redistribution note means they won't get their preferred hold-up position, and recent form at this trip on Good ground has been poor — the freshness concern alone warrants caution.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Onyeisi has managed a fourth five starts back but otherwise largely struggled for form; drawn in stall 15 carrying 130 lb, and back just three days after his latest run, the turnaround gives some pause despite experience over today's trip and going.

races.paceDynamic: Nibras Rainbow is the sole confirmed front runner in this 24-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead identified, is poised to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over 1m2f on Good ground at Navan. With Borora Aura and He Knows When likely to press forward from the prominent berths, there will be some early competition for position, but the pace is unlikely to be truly searching — meaning the race will be run at a rhythm that rewards those who can travel comfortably and produce a finish rather than those waiting furthest off the pace. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can get a clear run into the straight, as a moderate tempo will compress the field and limit the advantage of deep closers. The field holds substantially more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Deuteronomy, Onyeisi, Captain Con, Morning Approach, Trishuli River and several others are genuine hold-up horses who will be forced into midfield rather than their preferred rear berths, with Nibras Rainbow, Borora Aura and He Knows When the most likely to actually secure their natural positions near the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Nibras Rainbow gets a clean lead and the pace remains steady throughout, allowing the prominent horses to travel well within themselves.
scenarios.body: Nibras Rainbow sets an uncontested tempo that never truly quickens, keeping the field tightly grouped until the home straight where horses with finishing pace off a measured gallop thrive; prominent types who travel smoothly into contention are best placed to exploit this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pounce Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace causes a mid-race surge as prominent types push forward early in the straight, turning it into a test of sustained galloping ability.
scenarios.body: Borora Aura or He Knows When move to challenge Nibras Rainbow turning in, converting the race into an extended stamina test from 3f out; horses with a consistent record of finishing and whose natural style places them just off the pace are rewarded.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely fast enough to set the race up for those held up, and a true gap opens in the straight for late finishers.
scenarios.body: A rare scenario given the volume of redistributed hold-up types who will not get their preferred ground-saving berths, meaning genuine closers are few and cramped; any horse that does find clear daylight late — such as Millhone or Miss Crinshawn, whose form suggests a strong finish — could benefit, but the compressed field makes this difficult to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the 24-runner field produces early scrimmaging, traffic issues and a fractured pace that disadvantages those caught in the pack.
scenarios.body: In a race this large on Good ground, positional battles early can disrupt the rhythm for midfield horses, benefiting the few who secure clean rail positions or daylight from the front; Nibras Rainbow's established lead position and He Knows When's prominent style insulate them from the worst of the congestion.

watchPoints.text: Nibras Rainbow's ability to control the tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shape determinant — watch whether Borora Aura or He Knows When apply early pressure, as any sustained pace battle would fundamentally alter who benefits.

He Knows When returns from 784 days off the track; if the trainer has produced this horse fit, its natural prominent style is perfectly suited to this shape, but the layoff risk is extreme and punters should watch for any signs of greenness or ring-rustiness in the preliminaries.

Millhone's consistent placing record makes her a key marker in running — if she appears travelling easily in the midfield group with 3f to run, the race may be developing into a true test of finishing pace that suits her profile.

runners_data.name: Deetee
runners_data.note: Returns from a 706-day absence for Miss Natalia Lupini with just two prior runs both on Good ground yielding a placed effort, making fitness a genuine unknown; a prominent runner whose style suits this race shape but rustiness is a real risk.

runners_data.name: Highlander Addict
runners_data.note: Has a course-winning run over 17f to his name and several placed efforts on Good ground, but 1m2f looks sharp for a hold-up type whose best efforts have come over much longer; the 7lb claimer Robyn Donaghue-Leahy adds a weight advantage that helps.

runners_data.name: If Not For Grace
runners_data.note: Three runs all on Good ground, finishing 8th-13th-15th, with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish — a hold-up runner who has not yet shown the ability to see out these trips, and Cusack's yard is 0/3 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: It's Good To Talk
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins sends this 5-year-old back after 38 days, T14 showing 1/8 which indicates some stable activity; best run was a second over 2m on Heavier ground suggesting this 1m2f on Good is likely too sharp for a true staying hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Medadthebookie
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type whose sim-going record reads 0 wins from 6 on Good, with finishing positions drifting backward in longer races — the fade flag and consistent moderate finishes make improvement hard to project.

runners_data.name: Scorcher's Son
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 4-year-old has a single run to his name, finishing 7th over 8f on Good — the step up to 1m2f may suit but the form is thin and Declan McDonogh's booking is a mild positive signal from a powerful yard.

runners_data.name: Nugentstown Sue
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old running five days after her last outing, with a placed run deep in her record over 16f on Good ground; form figures of 14th and 11th in her last two suggest she will not trouble the judge here.

runners_data.name: Four Ball
runners_data.note: The 3-year-old's two runs have both produced mid-division finishes over 12f on Good ground; a true hold-up type operating in a field too full of closers to get a clear passage, and trainer Ciaran Murphy's 2/16 T14 record offers modest support at best.

runners_data.name: Giordano
runners_data.note: Two runs finishing 9th and 10th both on Good ground for Dermot Kilmartin, with a finish-fade flag and a genuine hold-up style that the crowded rear of this field makes even harder to deploy; natural position is at the back but the map reflects reality for this race.

runners_data.name: Gulf Beat
runners_data.note: Unraced debutant for Joseph O'Brien with no form to assess — the yard's firepower makes this horse relevant at face value, but the style is unknown and the unknown going tolerance adds uncertainty in a competitive 23-runner field.

runners_data.name: Heriot's Hope

runners_data.name: Legato
runners_data.note: Unraced first-timer for Michael Mulvany, drawn into a 23-runner maiden with no form clues available; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim offers a weight edge but style is entirely unknown and the yard's 1/12 T14 figure is unremarkable.

runners_data.name: Michinaga
runners_data.note: Charles Weld's 3-year-old has run twice on Good ground, finishing 6th over 12f and 9th over 9f — style is unknown but the form suggests a middle-distance type still finding his feet; 18 days since last run is a normal gap.

runners_data.name: Camelot Queen
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien's 3-year-old has placed at 8f, 10f and 10f on Good ground and is the only confirmed front-runner in the field — Wayne Lordan can dictate an uncontested gallop at 1m2f, and the mare's consistent placed form suggests she will not be easily caught if allowed to control the tempo.

runners_data.name: Sakoku
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's 3-year-old has a placed run at 13f on Good ground and showed ability; a genuine hold-up type shifted into midfield on the map due to the overcrowded rear, meaning Ben Coen will need to find a route through — the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.92 tempers expectations despite the underlying form being among the better in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Camelot Queen is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner maiden and, crucially, she faces no genuine pace rival to push her off her rhythm — she can dictate from the front at whatever tempo Wayne Lordan chooses, making this an unusually controlled lead scenario for such a large field. With Good ground confirmed all day at Navan over 1m2f and no challenger likely to contest her for the rail, she can set a sustainable gallop that leaves the field stretching out in her wake without burning early reserves. The field behind her is overwhelmingly populated by hold-up and midfield types, meaning the prominent berths just behind Camelot Queen are genuinely valuable and lightly contested — Handani and Royal Bones are best placed to exploit that gap. Several horses tagged as redistributed — including Giordano, Four Ball, Ben Lomond, and Sakoku — are natural hold-up types who will be pushed further back than suits them by the sheer volume of closers in the field, making their challenge dependent on ground they cannot easily make up. This race shape strongly favours a prominent racer or an on-pace stalker who can track Camelot Queen's controlled tempo and pounce before the true hold-up horses get into their stride.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Camelot Queen Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Camelot Queen bowls along uncontested and sets a fair but not punishing gallop, allowing her to quicken when pressed.
scenarios.body: She dictates every yard, and with no rival able or willing to challenge her early, she can conserve enough energy to repel challengers in the final two furlongs; the 1m2f trip and Good ground suit her proven form profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent racer tracks Camelot Queen throughout and picks her off inside the final furlong as the pace evens out.
scenarios.body: Handani and Royal Bones both have genuine prominent racing styles and the class/form to benefit from a well-run but not dawdling gallop; sitting a length or two off the leader with cover is ideal for a horse with Handani's placed form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Detonates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced unexposed types — Mississippi Shine, Twin Nation, or Gulf Beat — proves significantly superior and picks off the field from midfield.
scenarios.body: With several O'Brien and Lyons runners making their debut, the unknown form of these types makes an eye-catching winning run possible; Colin Keane on Mississippi Shine or Seamie Heffernan on Twin Nation adds strong jockey intent to the equation.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Run On Late
scenarios.trigger: If Camelot Queen sets an unexpectedly strong gallop that collapses in the straight, opening a late window for hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: This shape requires most redistributed hold-up types to navigate traffic in a large field late — a genuinely difficult ask when they cannot secure their natural position; Sakoku, who has shown a placed run at 13f on Good ground, is best placed of the closers to profit if it does materialise.

watchPoints.text: Handani and Royal Bones are the two prominent types best placed to latch onto Camelot Queen's back and attack her in the straight — watch both for how quickly they move to cover her in the first furlong.

Mississippi Shine (Keane/Lyons) and Twin Nation (Heffernan/Meade) are debutants with top-tier jockey bookings; if either is well fancied in the market drifting to short prices, treat as a serious dark-horse threat regardless of unknown style.

Camelot Queen's gallop tempo is the race's hinge — if she is allowed to creep along rather than stride out, the prominent stalkers gain an even bigger edge and the hold-up horses at the rear will never get rolling in time.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Giordano, Four Ball, Ben Lomond, Sakoku) will be bunched in midfield rather than at the rear where they want to be — watch for early traffic incidents or interference as 23 runners settle into position at the top of the straight.

Deetee returns from 706 days off the track and races prominently — if she emerges looking conspicuously well and jumps cleanly, the layoff is the only flag; a prominent style in a race with only one pace-setter means she could travel beautifully if fit.
